tagline: Farm highways over the wheat hills of Whitman County.
intro: This is a web of highways rather than one road, US 195 with state routes 26, 27, 272 and others, laid over the wheat-covered hills of Whitman County. It takes in Rosalia, Oakesdale and Tekoa, Colfax, the county seat, in its valley on the Palouse River, and Pullman and Uniontown.

The hills are silty loess, and Steptoe Butte stands up out of them, an island of quartzite more than 400 million years old. It made such an example that lone summits poking up through lava flows are now called steptoes.
season: State of Washington Tourism suggests spring for green fields or fall for golds and browns.

moments.title: Steptoe Butte
moments.text: The summit stands 3,612 feet up, about 1,000 feet above the country around it, and Mount Spokane is visible from it 70 miles to the north.

moments.title: Uniontown
moments.text: Its founder, Thomas Montgomery, had such a difficult personality that several businesses moved three miles north to the rival town of Colton.

moments.title: Palouse Falls
moments.text: Off on SR 261 the Palouse River drops into a canyon 377 feet deep cut by the Missoula floods, and in 1984 the ratepayers declined to pay for a dam above it.
